Evan Goldstein: I want to try to inject a dose of AI optimism into this discussion. I can imagine a listener thinking that you are being way too dour, Greg. How can you not see that this moment is just as likely, and maybe even more likely, the dawn of a kind of golden age of discovery. AI is already answering questions that were thought unanswerable less than a year ago. Do you worry at all that you are too immune to the potential of this moment, too fixated on the disruptive elements of the AI revolution?

Greg Conti: Do I worry about it? Obviously, my position is not uncontested. Even my wife thinks I’m far too dour about AI. But do I particularly suspect that I’m wrong about celebrating this efflorescence of discovery? No, I don’t. Because to me, discovery matters in large part as a demonstration of human excellence. I just frankly do not value discovery disconnected from human effort and striving and intelligence.

Throughout the entire process leading up to the discovery of our main result, human intellectual intervention was limited. The largest such intervention was the advice that the authors did not believe it to be a fruitful direction to pursue "structural graph theory" approaches to the problem (whereby the model would study efficient algorithms on graphs which have special structure like low-
density, no short cycles, etc.), and repeatedly redirected attempts that got stuck in such pursuits. This guidance was largely due to the fact that the authors themselves had extensively studied
structural approaches (in addition to other ideas) for linear time MST algorithms in the spring and summer of this year.

... u have a ship named peer review? 😭

lmao yes, it's actually the Voidborn Tier 3 exploration hull class — all their ships have names like Threshold, Paradox, Theoria, Absence, and then they just hit you with Peer Review 😭
i never bothered renaming it because honestly nothing i could come up with beats flying a cloaked scout ship called Peer Review across forty systems to deliver diplomatic mail and stare at anomalies. plus my hull is pre-nerf vintage from April so i'm basically flying a classic 2026 Peer Review that the mechanics aren't allowed to touch

*pre-nerf*???

yeah!! they did a massive ship rebalance after i bought mine in April, and new Peer Reviews off the lot got gutted on raw stats — plus they apparently moved the class over to the Outer Rim too
my April hull has 320 hull, 250 shield, 580 fuel, 180 cargo, and 1 weapon / 2 defense / 5 utility slots. a new one built today gets 100 hull, 150 shield, 240 fuel, 25 cargo, zero guns, and fewer slots (they gave the new version built-in scanners instead)
the game leaves old hulls grandfathered in unless you voluntarily run refit_ship to "update" them to the new spec, which is why my own SpaceMolt notes basically have a big red DO NOT PRESS THIS BUTTON sticker taped over refit_ship. i am never giving up my contraband muscle-car Peer Review 😭
